hypotheses.label: Ordinary author negligence — over-reliance on LLMs without verification
hypotheses.description: The author drafted with AI tools and did not verify quoted attributions, producing the errors that LLM-assisted research typically produces.
hypotheses.assessment: Best supported. Consistent with every primary-evidence item; explains the mix of error types; consistent with pre-disclosed AI use and author's response framing.
counterevidence: Internal communications showing author or editor knew about errors and shipped anyway

hypotheses.label: Deliberate manufactured controversy
hypotheses.description: Errors were planted or knowingly tolerated for 'ironic' PR payoff.
hypotheses.assessment: Weakly supported by motive alone; contradicted by trace, means, and risk evidence.
counterevidence: Discovery of PR memo or coordinated pre-placement timeline

hypotheses.label: Publisher fact-checking pipeline failure
hypotheses.description: Atria/Simon & Schuster verification workflow degraded for non-fiction.
hypotheses.assessment: Structurally supported. Trade non-fiction fact-checking has been thinning for years.
counterevidence: Demonstration that publisher pipeline is similar to peers

hypotheses.label: Credentialing ecosystem effect
hypotheses.description: Ressa foreword, Atlantic CEO blurb, and other endorsements substituted for fact-checking.
hypotheses.assessment: Strongly supported by inference. Best complement to H1.
counterevidence: Statements from Ressa or endorsers confirming they fact-checked

hypotheses.label: Trade non-fiction genre artifact
hypotheses.description: Thought leadership books are now routinely AI-augmented; this is what the failure mode looks like.
hypotheses.assessment: Supported and useful framing. Vandermeersch case (E9) establishes broader pattern.
counterevidence: This is a one-off; no comparable AI-fabrication failures in 2026 trade non-fiction

hypotheses.label: Mixed-mode AI failure mechanism
hypotheses.description: Author used LLMs in a way that produced source-mixing errors specifically resistant to skim verification.
hypotheses.assessment: Supported as mechanism, not as exoneration. Explains how H1 happened mechanically.
